in one discipline in a calendar year . In doubles, a Grand Slam may be achieved as a team or as an individual with different partners. Winning all four major championships consecutively but not within the same calendar year is referred to as a "non-calendar-year Grand Slam", while winning the four majors at any point during the course of a career is known as a "Career Grand Slam". [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The term Grand Slam is also attributed to the Grand Slam tournaments, [ 2 ] referred to as Majors, [ 3 ] and they are the world's four most important annual professional tennis tournaments. They offer the most ranking points, prize money, [ 3 ] public and media attention, the greatest strength and size of the field and, in recent years, the longest matches for men (best of five sets, best of three for the women). The tournaments are overseen by the International Tennis Federation (ITF), [ 4 ] rather than the separate men's and women's tour organizing bodies, the Association of Tennis

by the International Tennis Federation (ITF), [ 4 ] rather than the separate men's and women's tour organizing bodies, the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) and Women's Tennis Association (WTA), but both the ATP and WTA award ranking points based on players' performances in them. [ 5 ] The Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian Open in January, the French Open in late May to early June, Wimbledon in late June to early July, and the US Open in late August to early September, with each played over two weeks. The Australian and the US tournaments are played on hard courts , the French on clay court , and Wimbledon on grass court . Wimbledon is the oldest tournament, founded in 1877, followed by the US in 1881, the French in 1891 (major in 1925), and the Australian in 1905, but it was not until 1923 that all four were designated as "Official Championships". With the growing popularity of tennis, and with the hopes of unifying the sport's rules internationally, [ 6 ] the British and French tennis associations started discussions at their Davis Cup tie, and in October 1912 organized a meeting in Paris, joined by the Australasian , Austrian, Belgian , Spanish , and Swiss associations. [ 7 ] They subsequently formed the International Lawn Tennis Federation (ILTF), holding their first meeting in 1913, joined by the Danish, German , Dutch , Russian , South African, and Swedish organizations. [ 8 ] Voting rights were divided based on the perceived importance of the individual countries, with Great Britain's Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) receiving the maximum six votes. World Hard Court Championships , played on clay courts. World Covered Court Championships , played on an indoor wood surface. [ 10 ] The LTA was given the perpetual right to organize the World Grass Court Championships, to be held at Wimbledon, and France received permission to stage the World Hard Court Championships until 1916. [ 11 ] Anthony Wilding of New Zealand won all three of these World Championships in 1913. [ 12 ] The United States National Lawn Tennis Association (USNLTA) expressed disagreement over the power distribution within the ILTF and the designation of "World Championship" status to the British and French tournaments, and thus initially refused to join the Federation, choosing instead to be bystanders to their meetings. [ 13 ] [ 8 ] By the 1920s, with the World Covered Court Championships failing to attract top players and the growing success of American and Australian tennis, the ILTF worked to convince the USNLTA to join them, meeting their demand to drop the designation of "World Championships" from all three tournaments in March 1923, which led to the demise of both the World Covered Court Championships and the World Hard Court Championships. [ 10 ] [ 14 ] A new category of "Official Championships" was created for the national championships of Britain, France, Australia, and the US. [ 15 ] [ 16 ] By the 1930s, these four tournaments had become well defined as the most prestigious in the sport. [ 17 ] In 1933, Jack Crawford won the Australian , French , and Wimbledon Championships, leaving him just needing to win the last major event of the year, the U.S. Championships , to become the reigning champion of all four major tournaments, [ 18 ] a

Gould of The Reading Eagle , [ 19 ] and later that year by John Kieran of The New York Times , who stated that if Crawford won at Forest Hills it "would be something like scoring a grand slam on the courts, doubled and vulnerable." [ 20 ] [ 21 ] The term 'Grand Slam' originates from the card game contract bridge , where it is used for winning all possible tricks . In golf it was used for the first time to describe a total of four wins, specifically Bobby Jones ' achievement of winning the four major golf tournaments of the era, which he accomplished in 1930. [ 21 ] "Grand Slam" or "Slam" has since also become used to refer to the tournaments individually. [ 22 ] At the time, only amateur players were allowed to participate in the Grand Slam and other ILTF-sanctioned tournaments. [ 23 ] Amateur standing, regulated by the ILTF alongside its associated national federations, forbade players from receiving prize money, earning pay by teaching tennis, being contracted by promoters and playing paid exhibition matches, though expense payments were allowed along with certain monies from sporting goods companies or other benefactors. [ 23 ] Amateurs who "defected" to become professional were banned from competing in amateur tournaments and dropped from their national associations. The first major professional tour was established in 1926 by promoter C. C. Pyle with a troupe of American and French players, most notably Suzanne Lenglen , playing exhibition matches to paying audiences. [ 23 ] [ 24 ] Over the next

[ 23 ] [ 24 ] Over the next decades many other head-to-head tours were run and professional tournaments established, [ 25 ] with three, the U.S. Pro Tennis Championships , French Pro Championship and Wembley Championships , standing out, and considered to have been the professional majors . [ 26 ] By the 1950s, largely due to efforts of player/promoter Jack Kramer , this lucrative parallel circuit was luring in most of the star amateurs on the men's side, much to the ire of the ILTF and organizers of the Grand Slam tournaments. [ 27 ] It was an open secret that the top players who remained as amateurs were receiving undeclared under-the-table payments from tournament promoters, an arrangement tolerated by their national tennis associations to dissuade them from joining the pro ranks and secure their availability for the majors and Davis Cup. This system was derisively referred to as ' shamateurism ' [ 28 ] that was seen as undermining the integrity of the sport. [ 29 ] Ramanathan Krishnan and Roy Emerson , for example declined large contract offers from the professional promoters, with the latter stating that he was better paid in the amateur circuit. [ 30 ] Tensions over this status quo, which had been building for decades, finally came to a head in 1967. The first tournament open to professional tennis players played on Centre Court at Wimbledon, the Wimbledon Pro , was staged by the All England Lawn Tennis Club in August, [ 31 ] offering a prize fund of US$45,000. [ 32 ] The tournament was deemed very successful, with packed crowds and the play seen as being of higher quality than the amateur-only Wimbledon final held two weeks earlier. [ 35 ] The eventual backing of the USNLTA that came after a February 1968 vote forced the ILTF to yield and allow each nation to determine its own legislation regarding amateur and professional players, which it voted for in a special meeting in March 1968. [ 29 ] Even after the advent of the Open Era, players including John McEnroe and Chris Evert have pointed out that skipping the Australian Open was the norm because of the travelling distance involved and the inconvenient dates close to Christmas and New Year. [ 38 ] [ 39 ] There were also the contracted professional players who had to skip some major events like the French Open in the 1970s because they were committed to the more profitable pro circuits. The Australian Open is the first Grand Slam tournament of the year, played annually in late January and early February. [ k ] [ 49 ] The inaugural edition took place in November 1905 on the grass courts of the Warehouseman's Cricket Ground in Melbourne , Australia. It was held as the Australasian Championships until 1927 and thereafter as the Australian

the Warehouseman's Cricket Ground in Melbourne , Australia. It was held as the Australasian Championships until 1927 and thereafter as the Australian Championships until the onset of the Open Era in 1969, [ 50 ] passing through various venues in Australia and New Zealand before settling at the Kooyong Lawn Tennis Club in Melbourne between 1972 and 1987. [ 51 ] Since 1988, it has been played on the hard courts of the Melbourne Park sports complex, which currently uses GreenSet as its court manufacturer. [ 52 ] Managed by Tennis Australia , formerly the Lawn Tennis Association of Australia (LTAA), the tournament struggled until the mid-1980s to attract the top international players due to its distance from Europe and America and proximity to the Christmas and holiday season , [ 53 ] [ 54 ] but it has since grown to become one of the biggest sporting events in the Southern Hemisphere and the highest attended Grand Slam tournament, with more than 1,020,000 people attending the 2024

biggest sporting events in the Southern Hemisphere and the highest attended Grand Slam tournament, with more than 1,020,000 people attending the 2024 edition . [ 55 ] Nicknamed the "Happy Slam" [ 56 ] and billed as "the Grand Slam of Asia/Pacific", [ 57 ] it has become known for its modernity and innovation, being the first Grand Slam tournament to feature indoor play and install retractable roofs on its main courts, [ 58 ] the first to schedule night-time men's singles finals, [ 59 ] and the first to substitute electronic line calling for line judges , using an expanded version of the Hawk-Eye technology known as "Hawk-Eye Live". [ 60 ] The tournament was designated a major championship by the International Lawn Tennis Federation in 1923. [ 61 ] Today its draw hosts 256 singles players, 128 doubles teams, and 32 mixed doubles teams, with the total prize money for the 2025 tournament being A$ 96,500,000. The French Open, also known as Roland Garros, [ 63 ] [ 64 ] is the second Grand Slam tournament of the year, played annually in late May and early June. [ 65 ] A French championships closed event (restricted to members of French clubs) [ 66 ] was first held in 1891 on the sand courts of the Societé de Sport de Île de Puteaux, in Puteaux , Île-de-France, [ 67 ] [ l ] and changed venues over the years. In 1925 the French championships became a Grand Slam event for the first time. It was open to all amateurs and since 1928 has been held on clay courts at the Stade Roland-Garros in Paris, France. [ 66 ] [ 69 ] The venue is named "Roland Garros" after the pioneering French aviator . The Wimbledon Championships, commonly known as Wimbledon, [ 77 ] is the third Grand Slam tournament of the year, played annually in late June and early July. [ 78 ] It was first held in 1877 at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club , at the time located off Nursery Road in Wimbledon, London , England. [ 79 ] The tournament has always been contested at this club, which moved to its present site off Church Road in 1922 in order to increase its attendance capacity. [ 80 ] Wimbledon is organized by a committee of management consisting of 19 members, with 12 being club members and the remaining seven nominated by the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA). the remaining seven nominated by the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA). [ 81 ] [ 82 ] As the world's oldest tennis event, [ 83 ] it is widely regarded as the most prestigious tennis tournament, [ 84 ] and it is known for its commitment to longstanding traditions and guidelines. [ 85 ] It is one of few tournaments and the only Grand Slam event that is still played on grass courts, [ 86 ] tennis's original surface, and where "lawn tennis" originated in the 1800s . [ 87 ] Players are required to wear all-white attire during matches, [ 88 ] [ new archival link needed ] and they are referred to as "Gentlemen" and "Ladies". [ 89 ] There is also a tradition where the players are asked to bow or curtsy towards the Royal Box upon entering or leaving Centre Court when either the Prince of Wales or the monarch are present. [ 90 ] The tournament was given the title "World Grass Court Championships" by the International Lawn Tennis Federation between 1912 and 1923, [ 91 ] and was designated a major

the title "World Grass Court Championships" by the International Lawn Tennis Federation between 1912 and 1923, [ 91 ] and was designated a major championship following the abolition of the three ILTF World Championships. [ 61 ] Since 1937, the BBC has broadcast the tournament on television in the United Kingdom, [ 92 ] with the finals shown live and in full on television in the country each year. [ 93 ] The BBC's broadcast of the 1967 edition was among the first colour television broadcasts in the UK. [ 94 ] Today, the event has draws that host 256 singles players, 128 doubles teams and 32 mixed doubles teams, with the total prize money for the 2025 tournament being £ 53,500,000, [ 95 ] and 500,397 people attending the 2019 edition. [ 96 ] The tournament has some of the longest running sponsorships in sports history, having been associated with Slazenger since 1902, [ 97 ] and with the Robinsons fruit drink brand since 1935. [ 98 ] US Open [ edit ] Main article: US Open (tennis) Arthur Ashe Stadium , USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. The US Open is the fourth and final Grand Slam tournament of the year, played annually in late August and early September. It was first held in August 1881 on grass courts at the Newport Casino in Newport, Rhode Island , United States. [ 99 ] The tournament changed venues in its early years, [ 100 ] with each discipline continuing to be held separately at various venues until 1923, when the tournament settled at the West Side Tennis Club in Forest Hills, Queens , New York City. [ 100 ] In 1978, it moved to the hardcourts of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows , Queens, where it has been contested ever since. [ 100 ] [ 101 ] Organized by the United States Tennis Association (USTA), [ 102 ] previously known as the United States National Lawn Tennis Association (USNLTA) until 1920, [ 103 ] and as United States National Lawn Tennis Association (USLTA) until 1975, [ 104 ] it is the only Grand Slam tournament to have been played every year since its inception. [ 105 ] In 1997, Arthur Ashe Stadium , the largest tennis stadium in the world with a capacity of 23,771 spectators, [ 106 ] [ 107 ] was opened. [ 108 ] It is named after Arthur Ashe , the winner of the 1968 tournament—the first in which professionals were allowed to compete. [ 109 ] Over the years, the tournament has pioneered changes that other tournaments later adopted, including the introduction of a tiebreak system to decide the outcome of sets tied at 6–6 in 1970, [ 8 ] being the first Grand Slam tournament to award equal prize money to the men's and women's events in 1975, [ 8 ] the installation of floodlights in 1975 in

[ 111 ] The ILTF officially designated it as a major tournament in 1923. [ 10 ] Today, the event has draws that host 256 singles players, 128 doubles teams and 32 mixed doubles teams, with the total prize money for the 2020 tournament being US$53,400,000, [ 112 ] and a US television viewership of 700,000.
